newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent unmoved in quiet trade, gas oil slips.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent unmoved in quiet trade, gas oil slips.

text.p: IPE Brent futures retreated from a modest early gain to stand unchanged on the day by midsession with gas oil futures a little lower.
IPE August futures were unchanged at $17.76 a barrel by 1125 GMT. July gas oil futures were $1.75 lower at $161 a tonne.
"Everybody is sitting back and collecting their thoughts after Friday's expiry of the July (Brent) contract," one dealer said.
Brokers said a break of resistance at $17.90 a barrel was needed to trigger buying and move the market into a higher range.
Some pointed to continuing uncertainty over the Iraq/U.N. food-for-oil deal as providing a fundamental base from which the market could move higher.
But others feared Brent had been overbought in Friday's rally and players could be looking to shed their paper.
"I think Brent will come off when the market lives up a bit. There's a glut of it about," one broker said.
Baghdad's U.N. envoy, Nizar Hamdoon, said on Friday Iraq had no interest in delaying its oil sales, but wanted assurances on U.N. plans to distribute food and medicine bought with the proceeds.
Gas oil, meanwhile, was lower as fund selling in thin trade had an amplified effect.
"The mood is that we had a good week last week, and as we move down we seem to be finding solid support," one dealer said.
